newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Six months after the imposition of tax on deposits in foreign exchange, the finance ministry yesterday sent a circular on who was exempt from the 15 percent tax. Non permanent residents with forex deposits and drachma deposits originating from foreign exchange are exempt as are those holding a mortgage savings account in forex.
--The DIAS interbank capital movement system is expected to go into force as of September, giving the banking public the ability to move deposits and capital between banks with greater ease.

--The positions attributed to the Federation of Greek Industries on changes to the job market yesterday were only a partial representation of SEV's positions, culled from previous position papers, the federation told a news conference.

--Dramatic changes are in the pipeline for the Greek insurance market, with mergers planned as well as suspension of ailing firms. Estimates put the number of firms active in the sector by the end of the century at 40, down from 140 today. In life insurance, no more than 10 firms will be active.

--The Athens Stock Exchange continued to feel the effects of the problems yesterday at Katsoulis Securities, which is facing problems in meeting its 240 million drachma commitment to clients. The general price index closed down 0.67 percent.

--The country's deficits are presenting a better picture this first half-year, compared to the same period last year. According to the national economy ministry, the deficit was down 37.8 percent over the same period last year, totalling 1,025 billion drachmas this year from 1,650 billion drachmas last year.
--The Spraos committee is planning proposals to change taxation policy which will bump up tax revenues.
--Domestic flights will be up by 7.0 percent at Olympic Aviation, the administration announced yesterday. The real increases of some fares, however, will be up by as much as 20 percent.

--There has been an improvement in fiscal indicators for first half-1997 accroding to latest figures which show that budget inflows were up by 17.5 percent in comparison to the same period last year, while total spending increased only 0.3 percent. The increase in public inflows is due to a great degree to the 160 billion drachmas in revenues for the state from the OTE share offer.
--Industrial production increased 3.1 percent in April, positively affecting the results of the first quarter.

--The environment, town planning and public works ministry has clashed with the Macedonian Metro consortium over plans to develop a Thessaloniki subway system with Macedonian Metro claiming the ministry is determined to place the contract with a foreign consortium. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
